svg.text: Standard CVC with injectate sensor housing
PiCCO catheter available in different sizes:
Injectate sensor cable · Arterial connection cable ·

g.text: A known volume of cold saline is injected into the CVC. The cold fluid travels
through the right atrium and ventricle, across the pulmonary circulation,
and into the left heart before entering the systemic arterial system.
The arterial-catheter thermistor measures the blood temperature change
over time, generating a thermodilution washout curve.
Stewart–Hamilton analysis of this curve provides volumetric parameters
(fluid in the heart and lungs) and intermittent cardiac output.

svg.text: total blood in heart + pulmonary vessels
Calibration: thermodilution calibrates pulse contour analysis

g.text: Once calibrated by the thermodilution curve, the PiCCO monitor continuously
analyses the shape and area under the arterial pressure waveform, beat by beat.
A modified Wesseling algorithm calculates continuous stroke volume and
continuous cardiac output, and tracks dynamic variations in the pulse caused
